PREFACE

This preface should never be tasted. It talks about the author at some
length, thanks several people, and is not part of the story at all.




CHAPTER I.
The Arrival


It was a cold morning when the coach came down the long hill into the
village, and the whole street turned out to watch it arrive. The horses
steamed, the driver swore, and the children ran beside the wheels.

[Illustration: The coach on the hill

[_Copyright 1900 by Nobody._]]

“Who is it?” asked Mary, pressing her face to the glass.

“Nobody we know,” said her father, and went back to his newspaper.



CHAPTER II.


[Illustration]

The letter came on Tuesday. Nobody opened it until the evening, when
the lamps were lit and the fire was high.

    Roses are red,
    Violets are blue,
    This is a poem,
    And so are you.



CHAPTER III: Departure

She left before dawn, with one bag and no plan.

Book the first coach you can find, her mother had said, and do not look
back; and so she did not.



CHAPTER IV.



It was good to be home. The kettle sang and the dog slept by the door,
and nobody asked where she had been.

THE END

Some colophon that belongs to the printer, not the story.
